concepts.name: Structure, Councils, Assembly and Council composition and qualifications
concepts.description: How a State Legislature is built: unicameral and bicameral States, creation of a Council under Article 169, the Assembly's strength, term and composition, the Council's composition and tenure, and the qualifications for membership.
concepts.idea: A State Legislature is the Governor plus an Assembly (and a Council in six States), and each House is shaped by Articles 168 to 173.
concepts.rule: Part VI, Articles 168-212, covers the State Legislature, which consists of the Governor, the Assembly and, in bicameral States, the Council. Only six States have a Council (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka); under Article 169 Parliament can create or abolish one by an ordinary law, but only after the Assembly passes a special-majority resolution. The Assembly has 60 to 500 members (with lower minima for some small States), is directly elected, and lasts five years from its first meeting, extendable by one year at a time in a National Emergency. The Council has at most one-third of the Assembly's strength and at least 40 members, with one-third elected by local bodies, one-third by MLAs, one-twelfth each by graduates and teachers and one-sixth nominated by the Governor; it is permanent, one-third retiring every second year. Article 173 requires citizenship, an oath and a minimum age of 25 (Assembly) or 30 (Council), besides the qualifications Parliament adds.
concepts.example: A State that wants a second chamber needs an Assembly resolution by special majority first; Parliament then passes an ordinary law.

questions.q: In a State Legislative Council of 72 members, the number elected by teachers and the number nominated by the Governor are, respectively,
questions.e: Teachers elect one-twelfth of the Council (72/12 = 6) and the Governor nominates one-sixth (72/6 = 12).
w: One-twelfth is 6 for teachers, but nominees are one-sixth, i.e. 12, not 6.
Teachers elect one-twelfth (6), not one-sixth (12).
Teachers get 6 and nominees 12; reversing them wrongly gives teachers one-sixth.

questions.q: A State at present has no Legislative Council and wishes to have one. Which of the following sequences is constitutionally correct?
questions.a: The Assembly passes a resolution by special majority, and Parliament then makes a law by simple majority
o: The Assembly passes a resolution by special majority, and Parliament then makes a law by simple majority
Parliament passes a law by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, and the Assembly then ratifies it
The Assembly passes a resolution by simple majority, and Parliament then amends the Constitution under Article 368
The Governor recommends the creation to the President, who creates the Council by a notification
questions.e: Article 169: only after the Assembly's special-majority resolution (a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting) can Parliament create or abolish the Council, by an ordinary law which is not an Article 368 amendment.
w: Parliament cannot start on its own and no ratification by the Assembly follows.
The Assembly resolution needs a special majority, and the Parliament law is not an Article 368 amendment.
No presidential notification creates a Council; Parliament legislates under Article 169.

the date on which the Governor swears in the Chief Minister
the date of the Governor's proclamation calling the election

The oath before an authorised person is in Article 173.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the strength of State Legislative Assemblies:

1. The Constitution fixes the maximum strength at 500 and the minimum at 60.
2. The minimum strength is 40 for Mizoram and 46 for Nagaland.
3. The minimum strength for Arunachal Pradesh is 40.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 170 fixes the Assembly's strength at a maximum of 500 and a minimum of 60. Statement 2 is correct: the exceptions are Mizoram (minimum 40) and Nagaland (46). Statement 3 is incorrect: Arunachal Pradesh, like Goa, has a minimum of 30, not 40.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the organisation of State legislatures:

1. Most States are unicameral, with the Governor and the Assembly alone forming the Legislature, while a bicameral State adds the Council as a second House.
2. The Constitution requires every State to have two Houses.
3. Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the State Legislature.
4. Madhya Pradesh has a Legislative Council because the 7th Amendment Act of 1956 provided for it and the notification has been issued.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Most States are unicameral, with the Governor and the Assembly alone forming the Legislature, while a bicameral State adds the Council as a second House. Statement 2 is incorrect: each State may be unicameral or bicameral. Statement 3 is correct: Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the State Legislature. Statement 4 is incorrect: the notification has never been issued. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

3. The Council of Tamil Nadu had been abolished in 1986.
4. The Andhra Pradesh Council was the first to be abolished, in 1969.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: each by its own Abolition Act of 1969. Statement 3 is correct: Tamil Nadu Legislative Council (Abolition) Act, 1986. Statement 4 is incorrect: 1969 was Punjab and West Bengal; Andhra Pradesh's abolition came in 1985. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:

1. The 42nd Amendment froze the total number of seats and the territorial division at the 1971 census level up to the year 2000.
2. The 84th Amendment of 2001 extended the freeze on readjustment up to 2016.
3. The 87th Amendment of 2003 shifted delimitation to the basis of the 1991 census.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the 42nd Amendment froze seats at the 1971 census level up to 2000. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 84th Amendment extended the freeze up to the year 2026. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 87th Amendment shifted delimitation to the 2001 census. So exactly one statement is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statement 1 is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: statements 2 and 3 are both incorrect.
'All three' miscounts: only statement 1 is correct.

concepts.name: Disqualification, vacation of seats, oath, Speaker and sessions
concepts.description: Articles 188 to 192 and 174 to 180: grounds and decision of disqualification, vacation of seats, the oath, the Speaker's powers, summoning, prorogation and dissolution, and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
concepts.idea: Disqualification is decided by the Governor on the Election Commission's opinion (defection by the presiding officer), and the Speaker is the Assembly's elected, removable presiding officer.
concepts.rule: Article 191 disqualifies for an office of profit (Ministers excepted), unsound mind declared by a court, insolvency, loss of citizenship and disqualification by Parliament's law or the Tenth Schedule; under Article 192 the Governor decides but must act on the Election Commission's opinion, while defection is decided by the Speaker or Chairman subject to judicial review. A seat falls vacant on double membership, disqualification, resignation, sixty days' absence declared by the House, a void election, expulsion, election as President or Vice-President or appointment as Governor. Members take the oath before the Governor or his appointee. The Speaker maintains order, certifies Money Bills and has a casting vote only; he is removable by a majority of all the then members on 14 days' notice. The Governor summons and prorogues, with no more than six months between sessions, and dissolves the Assembly, while the Council is never dissolved.
concepts.example: An MLA charged with holding an office of profit has his case referred to the Governor, who must follow the Election Commission's opinion.

questions.q: An MLA is alleged to have become subject to a disqualification under Article 191(1) after his election. Who decides the question under Article 192?
questions.a: The Governor, who must obtain the Election Commission's opinion and act according to it
o: The Governor, who must obtain the Election Commission's opinion and act according to it
The President, acting on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers after consulting the Election Commission
The Speaker of the Assembly, whose decision is subject to judicial review
The High Court of the State, on a petition filed by the Speaker or any other member
questions.e: Under Article 192 the Governor's decision is final, but he must obtain the Election Commission's opinion and act accordingly.
w: The President decides such questions only for Members of Parliament.
The Speaker decides only defection cases under the Tenth Schedule.
No such reference to the High Court exists in Article 192.

questions.q: A newly elected member of the Legislative Assembly has not yet made the oath under Article 188. Which of the following is correct?
questions.a: He cannot vote or take part in the proceedings and does not become eligible for the privileges of the legislature
o: He cannot vote or take part in the proceedings and does not become eligible for the privileges of the legislature
He can vote on any motion before the House but cannot speak or move any motion until the oath is administered to him
He may take part in all debates and committees but cannot be counted towards the quorum of the House until he has been sworn in
He is entitled to the privileges of the legislature but not to his salary and allowances until the oath is taken by him
questions.e: Unless the oath is taken before the Governor or a person he appoints, a member cannot vote or participate and does not enjoy the privileges; sitting and voting meanwhile attracts a penalty of Rs 500 a day.
w: A member without the oath cannot vote at all.
The oath is a precondition for participation, not only for being counted in the quorum.
The privileges and immunities are themselves withheld until the oath is taken.

questions.q: A resolution to remove the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly must be moved
questions.a: after at least 14 days' notice and passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly
o: after at least 14 days' notice and passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly
after at least 7 days' notice and passed by a majority of the members present and voting in the Assembly
after at least 14 days' notice and passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Assembly
after at least 30 days' notice and passed by a majority of the members present and voting in the Assembly
questions.e: Article 179: removal by a resolution of a majority of all the then members (effective majority) on at least 14 days' notice; the same holds for the Deputy Speaker.
w: Both the notice period and the type of majority are wrong.
The majority required is an effective majority, not two-thirds of those present and voting.
The notice is 14 days and the majority is of all the then members.

questions.q: The last sitting of a session of a State Legislature was held on 10 March. By which date, at the latest, must the House next sit?
questions.e: Article 174(1): not more than six months may intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next, so the House meets at least twice a year.
w: That would be a three-month limit, not the six-month limit.
That gap would exceed the six-month limit.
That would be a two-month limit, not the six-month limit.

questions.q: A member of a State Legislature remains absent from all meetings of the House for sixty days without its permission. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.a: The House may declare the seat vacant, but the seat does not fall vacant automatically
o: The House may declare the seat vacant, but the seat does not fall vacant automatically
The seat falls vacant automatically at the end of sixty days of absence from all its meetings
The Governor declares the seat vacant on the recommendation of the Speaker after hearing the member
The Election Commission decides whether the seat is vacant after obtaining the member's explanation
questions.e: Article 190: a House may declare the seat of a member vacant if he is absent from all its meetings for sixty days without permission; it is not automatic.
w: The vacancy requires a decision of the House.
The Governor has no role in declaring the vacancy.
The Election Commission has no role in this vacancy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification of members under Article 191, which lists the grounds on which a person cannot be chosen as, or continue to be, a member:

1. A person holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any State Government is disqualified, including where the office is that of a Minister.
2. An undischarged insolvent is disqualified from being chosen or continuing as a member.
3. A person voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State is disqualified.
4. A person is disqualified for unsound mind on the certificate of any registered medical practitioner.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the office of Minister and offices exempted by the State legislature are excepted. Statement 2 is correct: a ground in Article 191. Statement 3 is correct: a citizenship ground. Statement 4 is incorrect: he must be of unsound mind and stand so declared by a competent court.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

Consider the following statements about the decision on disqualification under Article 192:

1. A question whether a member has incurred an Article 191(1) disqualification is referred to the Governor.
2. The Governor must obtain the opinion of the Election Commission and act according to it.
3. Article 192 also governs disqualification on the ground of defection, which is decided by the Governor on the Commission's advice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification on the ground of defection in a State Legislature:

1. Disqualification on the ground of defection is prescribed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and not by the Constitution.
2. The question is decided by the Speaker in the Assembly and by the Chairman in the Council, and not by the Governor.
3. In Kihoto Hollohan (1992) the Supreme Court held the presiding officer's defection ruling to be open to judicial review.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Constitution itself provides this ground through Article 191(2) and the Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985), not the Representation of the People Act. Statement 2 is correct: under the Tenth Schedule the Speaker or Chairman decides, not the Governor. Statement 3 is correct: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld the Schedule but held the presiding officer's decision subject to judicial review.

3. A member's resignation, addressed to the Speaker or Chairman, vacates the seat on the day it is sent, even if it has not been accepted.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cases in which a member of a State Legislature vacates his seat:

1. His election is declared void by a court.
2. He is expelled by the House.
3. He is elected as President or Vice-President of India.
4. He is appointed Governor of a State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 190 a seat is vacated when the member's election is declared void by a court. Statement 2 is correct: expulsion by the House vacates the seat. concepts.name: Council officers, procedure, Bills, assent and Money Bills
concepts.description: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council, the secretariat, adjournment, prorogation and lapse of Bills, quorum, voting, language, ordinary Bills and assent, rules of procedure and Money Bills.
concepts.idea: The Council is a dilatory chamber: an ordinary Bill is delayed for at most four months and a Money Bill for 14 days, and the Governor's veto is only suspensive.
concepts.rule: The Council elects its Chairman and Deputy Chairman, who resemble the Speaker and Deputy Speaker except that only the Speaker certifies Money Bills. Adjournment is ordered by the presiding officer and ends a sitting, prorogation by the Governor ends a session, and only the Assembly is dissolved, on which Bills pending in the Assembly lapse. Quorum under Article 189 is ten or one-tenth of the House, whichever is greater. An ordinary Bill from the Assembly can be delayed by the Council for four months in all (three plus one), there is no joint sitting, and a Council Bill rejected by the Assembly dies. The Governor may assent, withhold assent, return a non-Money Bill or reserve it for the President, and must assent when a returned Bill is passed again. A Money Bill originates only in the Assembly on the Governor's recommendation and the Council must return it within 14 days.
concepts.example: If the Council sits on an Assembly Bill beyond three months, the Assembly passes it again and, after a further month, it is deemed passed.

questions.q: In a State with a bicameral legislature, the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill rests with
questions.a: the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
o: the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
the Chairman of the Legislative Council of the State
the Governor, who recommends the Bill
the Advocate General of the State
questions.e: The Chairman's powers resemble the Speaker's, but whether a Bill is a Money Bill is decided finally by the Assembly Speaker.
w: The Chairman of the Council lacks this power; it is the one special power of the Speaker he does not share.
The Governor only gives the prior recommendation and cannot certify the character of the Bill.
The Advocate General only advises the State Government.

questions.q: A State Legislative Assembly has 120 members. The quorum required for transacting business is
questions.e: The quorum is ten members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is greater, counting the presiding officer; one-tenth of 120 is 12. The provision is in Article 189, not Article 188.
w: Ten is only the floor; one-tenth of 120 is 12, which is greater.
40 is one-third of the House, not a tenth.
60 is a majority of the House, not the quorum.

questions.q: On the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of a bicameral State, which of the following Bills lapses?
questions.a: A Bill passed by the Assembly and pending in the Legislative Council
o: A Bill passed by the Assembly and pending in the Legislative Council
A Bill pending in the Council that the Assembly has not yet passed
A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting the Governor's assent
A Bill passed by both Houses and returned by the President for reconsideration
questions.e: A Bill pending in the Assembly, or passed by it but pending in the Council, lapses; Bills pending only in the Council, awaiting assent, or returned for reconsideration do not.
w: A Bill still pending only in the Council does not lapse.
A Bill awaiting the Governor's or President's assent does not lapse.
A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration does not lapse.

questions.q: When the President returns a Bill reserved by the Governor for reconsideration, the House or Houses of the State Legislature must reconsider it within
questions.e: A Bill returned by the President must be reconsidered within six months.
w: One month is the second-stage period the Council has for an ordinary Bill.
Three months is the first-stage period for the Council on an ordinary Bill.
Fourteen days is the period for the Council to return a Money Bill.

questions.q: A member of the Assembly is unable to express himself adequately in the official language of the State, Hindi or English. Under Article 210 he may
questions.a: address the House in his mother tongue if the presiding officer permits
o: address the House in his mother tongue if the presiding officer permits
address the House in his mother tongue only if the Governor permits it in writing
speak in his mother tongue as of right, with no permission from the presiding officer
do so only if the Assembly has passed a resolution authorising it beforehand
questions.e: Business is transacted in the official language(s) of the State, Hindi or English, but the presiding officer may permit a member to speak in his mother tongue.
w: The permission comes from the presiding officer, not the Governor.
Permission is needed; it is not a matter of right.
No resolution of the House is required; the presiding officer's permission suffices.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council:

1. The Chairman is nominated by the Governor from among the members of the Council.
2. The Chairman addresses his resignation to the Deputy Chairman, while the Deputy Chairman addresses his to the Chairman.
3. The Chairman can be removed by a resolution of two-thirds of the members present and voting.
4. The Deputy Chairman vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the Council.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Council elects them from among its members (Article 182). Statement 2 is correct: Article 183. Statement 3 is incorrect: removal needs a majority of all the then members on 14 days' notice. Statement 4 is correct: Article 183.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the presiding arrangements of the Legislative Council:

1. When the office of Chairman is vacant, the Deputy Chairman performs his duties.
2. If both are absent from a sitting, a person nominated by the Governor presides.
3. While a resolution for his removal is under consideration the Chairman does not preside, but he may speak and take part and may vote in the first instance only.
4. A member of the panel of Vice-Chairmen nominated by the Chairman presides in the absence of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, with the Chairman's powers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 184. Statement 2 is incorrect: a person determined by the rules of procedure or fixed by the Council presides. Statement 3 is correct: Article 185. Statement 4 is correct: until a new panel is nominated.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the secretariat and officers of the State Legislature:

1. Each House of a State Legislature has its own separate secretarial staff.
2. In a bicameral State, posts common to both Houses may be created.
3. Recruitment and service conditions of the secretarial staff are regulated by a law made by Parliament.
4. The salaries and allowances of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State and are not voted annually.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 187(1). Statement 2 is correct: Article 187 permits it. Statement 3 is incorrect: they are regulated by State law, and until then by the Governor's rules after consulting the Speaker or Chairman. Statement 4 is correct: fixed by the State legislature and charged.

1. Adjournment sine die is ordered by the Governor.
2. A session consists of many sittings, and adjournment suspends work for a specified time such as hours, days or weeks.
3. After the presiding officer adjourns the House sine die, the Governor issues a notification proroguing it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the power of adjournment and adjournment sine die lies with the presiding officer. Statement 2 is correct: A session consists of many sittings, and adjournment suspends work for a specified time such as hours, days or weeks. Statement 3 is correct: the Governor may also prorogue a House that is in session.

Consider the following statements about the lapse of Bills on dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of a bicameral State:

1. A Bill pending in the Assembly lapses, whether it originated there or was transmitted by the Council.
2. A Bill pending in the Council that has not been passed by the Assembly lapses along with the Assembly.
3. A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting the assent of the Governor or the President does not lapse.
4. A Bill that the President has sent back to the Houses for reconsideration is treated as lapsed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Council is not dissolved, so such a Bill does not lapse. Statement 3 is correct: it is beyond the Houses. Statement 4 is incorrect: it does not lapse.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quorum and voting in a State Legislature:

1. Quorum and voting are dealt with in Article 189, whereas Article 188 deals with the oath.
2. In the absence of a quorum, the presiding officer is bound either to adjourn the House or to suspend its sitting until the quorum is made up.
3. The removal of the Speaker or Chairman is decided by a simple majority of members present and voting.
4. A few matters specified in the Constitution require an effective or special majority instead of a simple majority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 189 deals with voting and quorum, while Article 188 deals with the oath. Statement 2 is correct: in the absence of a quorum, the presiding officer must either adjourn the House or suspend its sitting until the quorum is made up. Statement 3 is incorrect: removal of the Speaker or Chairman needs a majority of all the then members (an effective majority), not a simple majority of those present and voting. Statement 4 is correct: other matters are decided by a simple majority of those present and voting, but a few matters specified in the Constitution need an effective or special majority.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Legislative Council and ordinary Bills passed by the Assembly:

1. The Council can detain an ordinary Bill for at most four months in all, three months in the first instance and one month in the second.
2. A deadlock arises if the Council rejects the Bill, proposes amendments the Assembly does not accept, or does not pass it within three months.
3. A Bill originating in the Council and rejected by the Assembly ends and becomes dead.
4. If the Council rejects the Bill, the Bill dies and the Assembly cannot pass it again.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 197 the Council can delay an ordinary Bill for at most four months, three in the first instance and one in the second. Statement 2 is correct: a deadlock arises if the Council rejects the Bill, proposes amendments the Assembly does not accept, or does not pass it within three months. Statement 3 is correct: the Council cannot override the Assembly, so a Bill originating in the Council and rejected by the Assembly is dead. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Assembly can pass it again, and if the Council rejects it a second time the Bill is deemed passed in the Assembly's form.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about assent to State Bills:

1. The Governor may give assent, withhold assent, return a Bill that is not a Money Bill, or reserve it for the President.
2. If a returned Bill is passed again, the Governor may still withhold his assent, since he has an absolute veto.
3. The Governor may reserve a Money Bill for the President but has no power to reserve a Bill on any other subject.
4. The Constitution makes it obligatory for the President to assent to a reserved Bill after it is passed again.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 200. Statement 2 is incorrect: he must assent, so he has only a suspensive veto. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Governor may reserve any Bill, not only a Money Bill (Article 200). Statement 4 is incorrect: the Constitution is silent on whether it is obligatory.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Money Bills in a State Legislature:

1. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly, on the recommendation of the Governor.
2. A Money Bill can be introduced by a private member with the Governor's consent.
3. The Council can only make recommendations and must return a Money Bill within 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.
4. If the Council does not return the Bill in 14 days, the Bill lapses.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 198. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is a Government Bill introduced only by a Minister. Statement 3 is correct: Article 198. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is deemed passed in the form passed by the Assembly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rules of procedure of the State Legislature:

1. Under Article 208(1) each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business.
2. Until the rules are made, the rules of Parliament apply to the State Legislature.
3. In a State with a Council, rules for communication between the Houses may be made by the Governor after consulting the Speaker and the Chairman.
4. Under Article 209 the Governor may regulate by ordinance the procedure in financial matters.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 208. Statement 2 is incorrect: the rules in force before the Constitution continue, modified by the Speaker or Chairman. Statement 3 is correct: Article 208(3). Statement 4 is incorrect: the State Legislature may regulate it by law. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor and the President in respect of Money Bills:

1. The Governor may assent to a Money Bill, withhold assent, or reserve it for the President.
2. The Governor may send a Money Bill back to the Legislature with a request to reconsider it.
3. The President, to whom a Money Bill has been reserved, may direct that it be sent back for reconsideration.
4. Normally the Governor assents to a Money Bill, since it was introduced with his prior permission.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Governor may assent to a Money Bill, withhold assent, or reserve it for the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: he cannot return it. Statement 3 is incorrect: he may only assent or withhold assent. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:

1. Ministers and the Advocate General may speak in either House and in committees of which they are members, but cannot vote unless they are members of that House.
2. The State legislature may decide to discontinue English as a floor language after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution.
3. For Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura the corresponding time limit is twenty-five years.
4. For Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Mizoram the corresponding time limit is forty years.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 177. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 4 statement(s) are correct.

'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Legislative Council occupies a weaker position against the Assembly than the Rajya Sabha against the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: On an ordinary Bill the Assembly can prevail by passing it a second time, and the Constitution provides no joint sitting of the two Houses of a State Legislature.

questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

w: This option treats Statement-II as correct but not explaining; Statement-II describes exactly why the Council is weaker.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; Statement-II describes exactly why the Council is weaker.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; Statement-II describes exactly why the Council is weaker.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-II: The Council can pass such a Bill a second time and compel the Assembly to accept it.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is incorrect: the second-passage override belongs to the Assembly, not the Council.

This option treats Statement-II as correct but not explaining; The second-passage route applies only to Bills originating in the Assembly.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; The second-passage route applies only to Bills originating in the Assembly.

concepts.name: Financial procedure, privileges and the Assembly versus the Council
concepts.description: Articles 202 to 207: the Annual Financial Statement, charged and voted expenditure, Appropriation Bills and the various grants; the collective and individual privileges of Article 194; and a comparison of the two Houses.
concepts.idea: The Assembly alone votes money, privileges protect Houses and members from obstruction, and the Council is subordinate in every sphere.
concepts.rule: The Annual Financial Statement of Article 202 shows charged and voted expenditure; charged items can be discussed but not voted, while demands for grants need the Governor's recommendation and can be accepted, refused or reduced. An Appropriation Bill cannot be amended to alter the amount or destination of a grant. Article 205 provides supplementary, additional and excess grants, and Article 206 a vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grant. Collective privileges include publishing proceedings, excluding strangers, punishing for contempt and freedom from court inquiry; individual privileges are freedom of speech, immunity from civil arrest during the session and 40 days before and after, and exemption from jury service. The Assembly is directly elected and mandatory, the Council indirectly elected and dependent on the Assembly for its existence.
concepts.example: A department that overspent last year's sanction needs an excess grant after audit, not a supplementary grant.

questions.q: Articles 202 to 207 provide a chain for legislative control over State finance. In the Constitution, the State's budget is described in Article 202 as the
questions.e: The word 'budget' is not used in the Constitution; Article 202 speaks of the Annual Financial Statement, showing estimated receipts and expenditure, charged and voted.
w: No such expression is used in Article 202.
The Consolidated Fund is a fund, not the name of the annual statement.
Demands for Grants are a later stage after the statement is laid.

questions.q: Which of the following items of State expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, and so can be discussed but not voted upon by the Assembly?
questions.a: Salaries and allowances of the Speaker of the Assembly
o: Salaries and allowances of the Speaker of the Assembly
A demand for grant of the Education Department
A supplementary grant for a service
The provision for a new scheme in the Annual Financial Statement
questions.e: Charged expenditure, such as salaries of constitutional authorities (including the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman) and interest on debt, is discussed but not voted.
w: Departmental demands for grant are voted expenditure.
A supplementary grant is put to the Assembly for its vote.
New schemes are voted expenditure, put as demands for grants.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Appropriation Bill of a State is correct?
questions.a: It authorises withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund, and no amendment can vary the amount or destination of a grant
o: It authorises withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund, and no amendment can vary the amount or destination of a grant
It is introduced before the demands for grants are voted, so that the Assembly can alter the demands afterwards by amending it
Money voted by the Assembly can be drawn from the Consolidated Fund by an executive order of the Governor without such a Bill
It may be introduced in either House, because the grants it covers have already been voted by the Assembly
questions.e: Article 204: after the grants are made, an Appropriation Bill is introduced to authorise withdrawal of voted and charged sums from the Consolidated Fund; no amendment may vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant, and no money can be withdrawn except under such a law.
w: The Bill follows the voting of the demands; it does not precede it.
Withdrawal needs the Appropriation law; an executive order is not enough.
It is a Money Bill-type measure introduced only in the Assembly.

questions.q: A department of a State Government spent in a past year more than the amount sanctioned by the Assembly, and the audit has been completed. The legislature regularises this through
questions.e: Article 205: an excess grant covers spending beyond the approved amount and is granted after the expenditure, following audit.
w: A supplementary grant covers a shortfall in the authorised amount for a service, before it is spent.
A vote of credit is for unforeseen, indeterminate expenditure.
A vote on account is a temporary approval while the budget process is incomplete.

questions.q: Which of the following is a privilege enjoyed by a House of a State Legislature collectively, and not by its members individually?
questions.a: Punishing members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt
o: Punishing members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt
Freedom of speech in the House, subject to the Constitution and the rules
Exemption from jury service and from appearing as a witness while the session lasts
Immunity from arrest in civil cases during the session and forty days on either side
questions.e: Collective privileges include punishing for breach or contempt, publishing and prohibiting publication of proceedings, and excluding strangers; freedom of speech, civil-arrest immunity and jury exemption are individual.
w: Freedom of speech is an individual privilege of members.
Jury exemption belongs to members individually.
Immunity from civil arrest belongs to members individually.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Annual Financial Statement and the voting of demands:

1. It is laid before the Legislature in the Governor's name and shows charged and voted expenditure separately.
2. Charged expenditure is put to the Assembly as a demand for grant and voted upon.
3. Voted expenditure is placed before the Assembly as Demands for Grants, which need the Governor's recommendation.
4. Charged expenditure may be discussed in the Assembly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 202. Statement 2 is incorrect: charged expenditure can be discussed but not voted. Statement 3 is correct: Article 203. Statement 4 is correct: discussion is allowed; only voting is barred.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about demands for grants and charged expenditure:

1. The Assembly may increase a demand for grant if the Government agrees.
2. Cut motions are of two kinds: policy cut and token cut.
3. Articles 202 to 207 together form the chain by which the Legislature controls State finance.
4. The Council can discuss the budget but cannot vote on the demands for grants.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it can accept, reject or reduce a demand, not increase it. Statement 2 is incorrect: there are three: policy cut, economy cut and token cut. Statement 3 is correct: Articles 202 to 207 together form the chain by which the Legislature controls State finance. Statement 4 is correct: voting is the exclusive privilege of the Assembly.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Appropriation Bills and additional spending:

1. An Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of the State for voted and charged expenditure.
2. An amendment altering the amount of a voted grant may be moved on the Appropriation Bill if the Speaker permits.
3. When the sum authorised for a service falls short, a supplementary grant is sought.
4. Expenditure on a new service that the budget never contemplated is met by an additional grant.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 204. Statement 2 is incorrect: no amendment can vary the amount or alter the destination. Statement 3 is correct: Article 205. Statement 4 is correct: Article 205.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the grants under Articles 205 and 206:

1. An excess grant is voted before the expenditure is incurred, as a forecast of overspending.
2. A vote on account is a temporary approval of expenses, usually for a short period, when the budget process is incomplete.
3. A vote of credit is for a known service with detailed estimates, so the executive has no discretion.
4. An exceptional grant is made for a special purpose outside the normal annual services.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it is granted after the expenditure, following audit. Statement 2 is correct: Article 206. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is for unforeseen, indeterminate expenditure and gives the executive wide discretion. Statement 4 is correct: Article 206.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bills dealing with State finance:

1. A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council.
2. A Financial Bill containing Money Bill matters along with other matters (Article 207(1)) can be introduced only in the Assembly, on the Governor's recommendation.
3. A Bill that would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State, but contains no Money Bill matters, cannot be passed by a House unless the Governor has recommended its consideration to that House.
4. A Bill that would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State cannot originate in the Council.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: Article 207(1). Statement 3 is correct: Article 207(3). Statement 4 is incorrect: such a Bill of the second category can originate in the Council; only the recommendation is needed at the consideration stage.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the collective privileges of a House of a State Legislature:

1. It may publish its debates and prohibit others from publishing them.
2. It may exclude strangers, including the media, and hold secret sittings.
3. Courts may examine procedural irregularities in the House's proceedings.
4. It may punish members as well as non-members for breach of privilege or contempt.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It may publish its debates and prohibit others from publishing them. Statement 2 is correct: It may exclude strangers, including the media, and hold secret sittings. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 212 bars courts from questioning them. Statement 4 is correct: members may also be suspended or expelled.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of a House in respect of its members and proceedings:

1. It is entitled to be informed immediately of the arrest, detention or imprisonment of a member.
2. It may summon witnesses, call for documents and conduct inquiries through committees.
3. Courts cannot inquire into the proceedings of a House or its committees on the ground of procedural irregularity, though review for illegality or mala fides remains possible.
4. In a criminal matter, legal process may be served within the precincts of the House without the presiding officer's permission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: a House is entitled to be informed immediately of the arrest, detention or imprisonment of a member. Statement 2 is correct: it may summon witnesses, call for documents and conduct inquiries through committees. Statement 3 is correct: Article 212 bars courts from questioning the validity of proceedings on the ground of irregularity of procedure; review for illegality or mala fides survives under settled case law (Raja Ram Pal, 2007). Statement 4 is incorrect: no arrest or legal process, civil or criminal, may be executed within the precincts without the presiding officer's permission.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the individual privileges of members of a State Legislature:

1. No member is liable in any court for anything said or any vote given in the legislature or its committees, subject to the Constitution and the rules of the House.
2. In civil proceedings a member is protected from arrest while the session lasts and for 30 days on either side of it.
3. The immunity from arrest extends to criminal cases and preventive detention.
4. Members are exempt from jury service and may refuse to appear as witnesses while the legislature is in session.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: No member is liable in any court for anything said or any vote given in the legislature or its committees, subject to the Constitution and the rules of the House. Statement 2 is incorrect: the period is 40 days before and after. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is confined to civil cases. Statement 4 is correct: Members are exempt from jury service and may refuse to appear as witnesses while the legislature is in session.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Assembly and the Council:

1. A no-confidence motion carried in the Council obliges the Council of Ministers to resign.
2. The Council cannot amend or reject a Money Bill and can only delay it by 14 days.
3. The Council does not take part in the election of the President of India or of the State's Rajya Sabha members.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Assembly. Statement 2 is correct: Article 198. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the privileges of State legislatures:

1. Article 194 privileges are broadly modelled on those of the House of Commons of the United Kingdom.
2. They are classified into collective privileges and individual privileges.
3. The privileges extend to the Governor as an integral part of the State legislature.
4. The privileges are extended to the Advocate General and State Ministers who may speak in the House.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 194 privileges are broadly modelled on those of the House of Commons of the United Kingdom. Statement 2 is correct: They are classified into collective privileges and individual privileges. Statement 3 is incorrect: they do not extend to the Governor. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about comparing the Assembly and the Council:

1. The minimum age for membership is 25 years for the Assembly and 30 years for the Council.
2. The minimum strength of the Council is 60, the same as that of the Assembly.
3. The Governor can dissolve the Council on the advice of the Chief Minister, as he can the Assembly.
4. Members of the Council are directly elected, while members of the Assembly are indirectly elected.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 173. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Council's minimum is 40. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Council is a permanent House not subject to dissolution. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Assembly is directly elected; the Council is indirectly elected or nominated. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Articles dealing with State financial procedure:

1. Article 202 deals with the Annual Financial Statement.
2. Article 203 deals with Appropriation Bills.
3. Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants are in Article 205.
4. Special provisions as to financial Bills are in Article 208.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 202. Statement 2 is incorrect: Appropriation Bills are in Article 204; Article 203 is the procedure on estimates. Statement 3 is incorrect: they are in Article 206; Article 205 has supplementary, additional and excess grants. Statement 4 is incorrect: they are in Article 207; Article 208 deals with rules of procedure. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A House of a State Legislature may exclude strangers and hold secret sittings.
Statement-II: A House has the right to be informed immediately of the arrest of a member.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct collective privileges, but they are separate privileges and neither explains the other.
w: This option treats Statement-II as explaining Statement-I; They are independent privileges.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; They are independent privileges.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; They are independent privileges.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A member cannot be held liable in a court for a vote given in a committee of the legislature.
Statement-II: The freedom of speech of members is subject to no restriction from the Constitution or the rules of the House.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: A member cannot be held liable in a court for a vote given in a committee of the legislature. Statement-II is incorrect: the freedom is subject to the provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating procedure.
w: This option treats Statement-II as explaining Statement-I; The freedom is subject to the Constitution and House rules.
This option treats Statement-II as correct but not explaining; The freedom is subject to the Constitution and House rules.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; The freedom is subject to the Constitution and House rules.

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Supplementary grant
B. Additional grant
C. Vote on account
D. Vote of credit

List-II
1. Temporary approval of expenses when the budget process is incomplete
2. Authorised amount for a service proves insufficient
3. Unforeseen and indeterminate expenditure giving the executive wide discretion
4. A new service not contemplated earlier
questions.e: Article 205: a supplementary grant for insufficiency and an additional grant for a new service; Article 206: a vote on account is temporary approval and a vote of credit covers unforeseen, indeterminate expenditure.
w: Items C and A are interchanged: C belongs with 1 and A with 2.
Items D and C are interchanged: D belongs with 3 and C with 1.
Items B and D are interchanged: B belongs with 4 and D with 3.
